about: Hand-authored ground truth for bench/bench_overlap_skipgram.py's precision arm, over the 15 numbered chapters of the digital-twins book, after #180's two fixes. `label` follows 2026-08-13-overlap-gate/labels.json's rubric: `tp` = reuse a reviewer would require fixing, `fp` = a finding no reviewer would act on. Rationales carry no extended source text; each passage is locatable from `draft` and `line` in skipgram_precision.json.

corpus.note: finding ids are sha256(citekey, page, fragment), so a re-parse or a page shift invalidates this file rather than silently half-matching it. tokenizer_version 2 is #180's; a run against a version-1 index reports every one of these labels as stale.

finding_classes.stock-phrase-echo: The matched words are the field's stock phrasing -- a sentence any survey in the area writes. Distinct from canonical-definition in that there is no definition being reproduced, only common vocabulary in a common order.
finding_classes.third-party-echo: A canonical definition, or one passage's reuse, matched against a paper other than the one the draft credits -- including the volume that contains the cited chapter. `cites_source` cannot tell this from real uncredited reuse.
finding_classes.attributed-quotation: Quoted with quote marks and attributed. Legitimate scholarship. Tier 2's `quoted` flag misses several of these because a skip-gram window straddles the opening quote mark.
finding_classes.unquoted-close-reuse: The draft reproduces the source's own wording without quotation marks, citing it. A reviewer would require quote marks, so this is a true positive -- but on this book both instances are passages the exact tier already reports.
